items.stem: A churn dataset is 95% non-churn. Why is accuracy a poor metric here?

options.text: A model predicting 'never churns' scores 95% while being useless
options.rationale: Correct: accuracy rewards the majority class on imbalanced data.

options.text: Accuracy cannot be computed for classification
options.rationale: It can be computed; it is just misleading here.
That is unrelated to the imbalance problem.

items.explanation: Correct: accuracy rewards the majority class on imbalanced data.

items.stem: Which TWO signs point to overfitting? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Training error is very low but validation error is much higher
options.rationale: Correct: a large train/validation gap signals overfitting.

options.text: Performance drops sharply on new, unseen data
options.rationale: Correct: poor generalisation is the defining symptom.

options.text: Training and validation error are both high and close
The model is too simple to fit the training data

items.explanation: Correct: a large train/validation gap signals overfitting.

items.stem: You tune a model by repeatedly checking the test set and picking the best. What is the flaw?

options.text: The test set leaks into tuning, so its score no longer estimates generalisation
options.rationale: Correct: the test set must stay untouched until final evaluation.

options.text: Testing many times improves the true accuracy
options.rationale: It inflates the reported score, not the true accuracy.

options.text: There is no flaw if the model is simple
options.rationale: The leakage flaw is independent of model simplicity.

options.text: The training set becomes too small
options.rationale: Repeated test checks do not shrink the training set.

items.explanation: Correct: the test set must stay untouched until final evaluation.
